📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Scope Core Definition

Scope the part of the program from where a particular Python object can be referenced.

Python Language Overview Key Concept

Python is a dynamic, interpreted or a byte code-compiled language.

Data Types In Python Key Concept

Data types define the type of a variable that represents the type of data that can be stored in a variable and the kind of operations that can be done on it.

Aliasing In Python Key Concept

Each identifier is associated with the memory address of the object to which it referring to.

Expressions In Python Key Concept

Like in C or C++, a combination of operands and operators is called an expression.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

1.2 Python Language Overview

  • Python is a dynamic, interpreted or a byte code-compiled language.
  • This means that prototyping can be very quick while testing the code.
  • As you code in Python, you shall look at it like procedural at times or object-oriented.
  • One doesnot have to bother about the type declarations of variables, parameters, functions, or methods in code you write.

1.3 Data Types in Python

  • Data types define the type of a variable that represents the type of data that can be stored in a variable and the kind of operations that can be done on it.
  • Data Type Description Numeric int, float, complex Sequence list, tuple range Mapping dict Set set, frozenset Text str Binary bytes, bytearray, memoryview Numeric Types: int: Used to represents whole numbers (e.g.: 2, -15, 0).
  • float: Used to represents decimal numbers (e.g.: 2.14, -0.8, 8.0).
  • complex: Used to represents complex numbers in the form a + bk, where a and b are floats and k is the imaginary section (e.g.: 6 + 8k, -1k).

1.4 Classes and Objects in Python

  • Python is an object-oriented language and classes form the basis for all its data types.
  • Classes are a means of bringing together data and functionality together.
  • Each class encapsulates data and behaviour (methods) into a single entity.
  • This structure allows you to model real-world objects and create organized, reusable code.

1.5 Aliasing in Python

  • Each identifier is associated with the memory address of the object to which it referring to.
  • An identifier can be associated with one type of object initially and later it can be reassigned to another object that is of the same or different type.
  • Modifying any one of the the list will affect the other.
  • Aliasing can lead to unexpected side effects if not handled carefully.

1.6 Expressions in Python

  • Like in C or C++, a combination of operands and operators is called an expression.
  • The expression produces some value or result after being interpreted by the Python interpreter.
  • It combines operators, variables, literals, and function calls to produce a value.
  • The programming language uses distinct expressions for various requirements.

1.7 Control Flow

  • Program execution happens sequentially in Python wherein the Python interpreter reads a code written by you line by line from top to bottom with each statement interpreted from left to right and.
  • The interpreter executes operations and functions in the order that it reads which is what the control flow signifies.
  • Not every program shall follow this pattern since the program shall also encounter conditional statement and based on this outcome, the control gets transferred to the desired statement.
  • Without control flow expressions, a program is simply a list of statements that are sequentially executed.

1.8 Looping / Repetition

  • Understanding loops is essential for any python programmer as these provide a powerful tool to automate code logic and process data.
  • Python being popular programming language, offers several loop structures to iterate over sequences and execute repetitive tasks efficiently.
  • These are also referred to as repetition statement used to repeat a block of code statements.
  • Python has two loops structures which are: for loop while loop 1.8.1 for loop It is used to iterate over a sequence that can be a list, tuple, dictionary, or a set.

1.9 Functions

  • A function is a block of reusable code that performs a specific task.
  • This task is generally one which is used multiple times to develop an application in Python.
  • Suppose we need to create a program to compute area of a given land or the volume of a box.
  • The idea is to organize code, make it more readable, and avoid repetition of the same code statements.
